newsitem.title: USA: GE Investments chief aims for high growth.
newsitem.headline: GE Investments chief aims for high growth.

text.p: The new president of GE Investments hopes to keep the company on the same high-growth path as his predecessor, he told Reuters on Wednesday.
"My selection is one that does not signal a lot of change," said John H. Myers, 51, who earlier was named president of GE Investments.
The General Electric Co unit manages some $56 billion in assets.
Myers was previously executive vice president of GE Investments. He succeeds Dale F. Frey, who is retiring after 40 years with GE.
Myers credited Frey with building the company from a $16 billion operation in 1984.
GE Investments manages both the pension fund of GE employees, which is worth about $30 billion, and various assets for institutional clients.
"We won't offer products that we don't believe in ourselves for our own investment purposes," said Myers.

"I see us hopefully continuing to fuel our growth engine. We will announce tomorrow the introduction of an emerging-markets product for institutions, which we are doing with one of our largest clients," he said without elaborating.
Myers previously oversaw the company's private equity, fixed-income, real estate and venture capital investments.
GE Investments is the nation's eighth-biggest independent manager of tax-exempt assets and has $11 billion in mutual fund assets under management.
